title: Helpdesk review sampling bias research: seeing the misses a queue hides
excerpt: A bounded examination of routine-only samples, boundary cases, and why article quality review needs more than easy tickets.
question: How should a helpdesk review sample be structured so that routine accuracy does not hide failures at escalation, privacy, or ownership boundaries?
focus: quality-review sampling across routine, boundary, returned, and high-consequence helpdesk cases
finding: a useful sample preserves the conditions that change the safe action, because an easy-ticket majority can conceal the few cases where authority and evidence matter most
limitation: the public-source design does not estimate a statistically representative miss rate for any queue
